name: Five Times Life Nearly Ended
description: The five great extinctions in Earth's past, what caused them, who survived, and why scientists fear a sixth is under way today.

checkpoints.name: Shells, then ice
checkpoints.note: Animals burst into variety in the Cambrian seas. Then the first great extinction strikes as ice spreads and the sea falls, killing much of the life in shallow waters.

checkpoints.name: The fall of the fish age
checkpoints.note: Armoured fish dominate the Devonian seas and forests spread on land, but a long series of extinctions hits reefs and sea life hard.

checkpoints.name: The Great Dying
checkpoints.note: Siberian lava floods, a greenhouse world and starved oceans bring the worst extinction known, about 252 million years ago, ending most life on Earth.

checkpoints.name: Dinosaurs rise and fall
checkpoints.note: Dinosaurs benefit from a Triassic extinction, rule for 135 million years, and lose out to a huge asteroid impact and volcanic eruptions, while small mammals survive.

checkpoints.name: Is a sixth under way?
checkpoints.note: After warming spikes and cooler ages, humans arrive, and many scientists say hunting, habitat loss and climate change are driving species out faster than normal.
